questions.q: Why did Alan refuse "Bonnie House of Airlie" as the whistled signal?
choices: Any ploughman might whistle it by accident
It was a Whig song that he could never abide
David could never whistle it in tune
It was too long to whistle in the dark
questions.evidence: any ploughman might whistle it by accident

questions.q: Where was Alan to wait after dark until he heard David whistle?
choices: In the fields by the roadside near Newhalls
In the den down on the sea-shore near Carriden
Behind the town-hall of Queensferry
In the little wood above Limekilns
questions.evidence: he should lie in the fields by the roadside near to Newhalls

questions.q: As the morning went on in Queensferry, why did David grow more and more worried?
choices: He had no proof of his rights, or even of who he was
He had seen soldiers searching every house on the street
He feared his uncle was waiting for him at the harbour
He had lost the paper with Mr. Rankeillor's address
questions.evidence: no clear proof of my rights, nor so much as of my own identity

questions.q: Why could David not bring himself to ask anyone for Mr. Rankeillor's house?
choices: He was ashamed of his rags and thought they would laugh
He did not speak the Lowland way of the townspeople
Alan had warned him to speak to no one in the town
He was afraid the lawyer was his uncle's close friend
questions.evidence: I thought shame even to speak with them in such a pickle of rags and dirt

questions.q: How did David finally meet Mr. Rankeillor?
choices: The lawyer noticed him outside his own house and asked his business
A kind lass from the harbour led him straight to the lawyer's office
He knocked at a dozen doors until a servant fetched the lawyer
Mr. Campbell the minister happened to be passing and took him there
questions.evidence: he came straight up to me and asked me what I did

questions.q: The house had walls "new-harled." Using the note in the chapter, what does that mean?
choices: Newly rough-cast
Freshly painted white
Recently built of brick
Covered in climbing ivy

questions.q: Why did Mr. Rankeillor speak a line of Latin to David early in their talk?
choices: To test whether David was really an educated young man
To show off to his clerk, who was listening at the door
To give David a secret warning that his uncle was nearby
Because he had forgotten how to say it plainly in English
questions.evidence: his scrap of Latin had been set to test me

questions.q: Where did David say his father worked?
choices: As the schoolmaster of Essendean
As minister of a church in Angus
As a lawyer in the town of Edinburgh
As a farmer near the House of Shaws
questions.evidence: My father was Alexander Balfour, schoolmaster of that place

questions.q: Who did David say held the papers that could prove who he was?
choices: Mr. Campbell, the minister
His uncle, Ebenezer Balfour
Captain Hoseason of the brig
Mr. Rankeillor's clerk
questions.evidence: they are in the hands of Mr. Campbell, the minister

questions.q: Rankeillor points out "a considerable hiatus" of nearly two months between the shipwreck and today. What is a "hiatus" here?
choices: A gap of time that is not accounted for
A large sum of money that has been lost
A legal paper that has to be signed
A long voyage across a stormy sea
questions.evidence: Here is a considerable hiatus, Mr. Balfour, of near upon two months

questions.q: Why did David at first hold back from telling Rankeillor his story?
choices: He had suffered from trusting before, and thought the lawyer was his uncle's man
He was too hungry and tired to talk at all until he had eaten a good proper meal
He was afraid Rankeillor would send at once for the soldiers in the town
He had promised Alan never to tell anyone anything about the journey
questions.evidence: I have already suffered by my trustfulness

questions.q: What did Uncle Ebenezer claim had happened to David when Mr. Campbell came asking for him?
choices: He had gone to Europe to finish his education
He had joined the army and gone to fight in France
He had drowned in the sea off the Isle of Mull
He had gone back home to Essendean to live
questions.evidence: you had started for the continent of Europe, intending to fulfil your education

questions.q: What story did Captain Hoseason bring, which made everyone stop searching?
choices: That David had drowned
That David was in Leyden
That David had run away
That David was in prison
questions.evidence: comes Captain Hoseason with the story of your drowning

questions.q: How did Rankeillor listen while David told his whole story?
choices: With his eyes closed, yet hearing and remembering every word
Writing every single detail down quickly in his paper book
Walking up and down the room and asking many questions
Interrupting often to argue about the law with David
questions.evidence: he listening with his spectacles thrust up and his eyes closed

questions.q: Why did Rankeillor pretend not to hear Alan's name and call him "Mr. Thomson"?
choices: As a lawyer he wished not to know officially about a wanted man
He was truly hard of hearing and could not catch Highland names
He had once known a real Mr. Thomson who looked much like Alan
He wanted to write the story down later and needed simpler names
questions.evidence: he must have heard the name all too clearly

questions.q: What name did David give to Cluny in his story?
choices: Mr. Jameson, a Highland chief
Mr. Glen, a gentleman of Appin
Mr. Thomson's kinsman
Mr. Stewart of the Cage

questions.q: What did Rankeillor think of David's loyalty to "Mr. Thomson"?
choices: He was right to stick by him, since Alan had stuck by David
He was foolish to trust a Highlander who was wanted for murder
He ought to give Alan up to the law to clear his own name
He should send Alan away at once and never see him again
questions.evidence: you are doubtless quite right to adhere to him; indubitably, he adhered to you

questions.q: What did Rankeillor do at the end of the chapter when he saw David look at his rags?
choices: Had a plate laid for dinner and gave him soap and his son's clothes
Gave him a few shillings and sent him out to buy new clothes in the town
Told him to wait in the dusty chamber while he fetched a tailor
Sent him off to the inn by the harbour to wash and rest a while
questions.evidence: laid out some clothes that belonged to his son

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: David finds Mr. Rankeillor and wins his trust and help
David is turned away by the lawyer and must go back to Alan
David meets his uncle in Queensferry and has him arrested
David proves who he is by showing Mr. Campbell's letters
questions.evidence: you are near the end of your troubles
